Both PRs are built off the identical base blob (243eef5ae6) and rewrite the exact same lines (~141-155) of cancel(), so they textually conflict. #2493 simply deletes the 'send an error response to indicate cancellation' block and updates server.py's _handle_request comment/log to match ('per spec receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request'), covering the case where the client already sent a CancelledNotification. #2514 touches the same block but goes further: it imports CancelledNotificationParams and removes the stale '# pragma: no cover' marker on the _entered guard, indicating it replaces the deleted response-sending code with logic that emits a notifications/cancelled message for the request-timeout and caller-initiated-cancellation cases (i.e. scenarios where the peer does NOT already know the request was cancelled and needs to be told). #2493 never touches those cases and leaves no replacement notification, so merging #2514 alone reproduces #2493's fix (no more erroneous response) while also closing the remaining gap; merging #2493 alone would leave timeout/caller-cancellation silent with no peer notification.

members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: post_writer() is spawned into the task group with tg.start_soon() without waiting for it to actually be ready to receive from write_stream_reader, so a message sent immediately after spawn can race ahead of the reader and get dropped/hang. Both PRs fix this by adding a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to post_writer and calling `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context manager(s), so the caller can use `tg.start()` and block until post_writer is truly ready.
